title: The passwords at the gates of the archons
source_text: Εἰ δέ τις βούλεται καὶ τὰ πλάσματα τῶν γοήτων ἐκείνων μαθεῖν, δι᾿ ὧν ἐβουλήθησαν μὲν ὑπάγειν ἀνθρώπους ἑαυτῶν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ ὡς ἀπόῤῥητά τινα ἔχοντες οὐ πάνυ δ᾿ ἐδυνήθησαν, ἀκουέτω ὃ διδάσκονται λέγειν μετὰ τὸ διελθεῖν ὃν ὀνομάζουσι „φραγμὸν κακίας“, πύλας ἀρχόντων αἰῶνι δεδεμένας· „βασιλέα μονότροπον, δεσμὸν ἀβλεψίας, λήθην ἀπερίσκεπτον ἀσπάζομαι, πρώτην δύναμιν, πνεύματι προνοίας καὶ σοφίᾳ τηρουμένην· ἔνθεν εἰλικρινὴς πέμπομαι, φωτὸς ἤδη μέρος υἱοῦ καὶ πατρός· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι, ναὶ πάτερ, συνέστω.“ καί φασι τῆς ὀγδοάδος τὰς ἀρχὰς ἐντεῦθεν εἶναι. εἶθ᾿ ἑξῆς διδάσκονται λέγειν διερχόμενοι ὅν φασιν Ἰαλδαβαώθ· „σὺ δὲ μετὰ πεποιθήσεως πρῶτε καὶ ἕβδομε γεγονὼς κρατεῖν Ἰαλδαβαὼθ, ἄρχων λόγος ὑπάρχων νοὸς εἰλικρινοῦς, ἔργον τέλειον υἱῷ καὶ πατρὶ, χαρακτῆρι τύπου ζωῆς σύμβολον ἐπιφέρων, ἣν ἔκλεισας αἰῶνι σῷ πύλην κόσμῳ ἀνοίξας. παροδεύω τὴν σὴν ἐλεύθερος πάλιν ἐξουσίαν· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι, ναὶ πάτερ, συνέστω.“ φασὶ δὲ τῷ λεοντοειδεῖ ἄρχοντι συμπαθεῖν ἄστρον τὸν Φαίνοντα. εἶτα οἴονται τὸν διελθόντα τὸν Ἰαλδαβαὼθ καὶ φθάσαντα ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰα (ὼ) δεῖν λέγειν· „σὺ δὲ κρυπτομένων μυστηρίων υἱοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἄρχων νυκτοφαὴς δεύτερε Ἰαὼ καὶ πρῶτε δέσποτα θανάτου, μέρος ἀθώου. φέρων ἤδη τὴν ἰδίαν ὑπήνην σύμβολον, παροδεύων σὴν ἕτοιμος ἀρχήν· κατίσχυσας τὸν ἀπὸ σοῦ γενόμενον λόγῳ ζῶντι· ἡ χάρις συνέστω, πάτερ, συνέστω.“ εἶθ᾿ ἑξῆς τὸν Σαβαὼθ, πρὸς ὃν οἴονται λέξειν· „πέμπτης ἐξουσίας ἄρχων, δυνάστα Σαβαὼθ. προήγορε νόμου τῆς σῆς κτίσεως χάριτι λυομένης, πεντάδι δυνατωτέρᾳ, πάρες με, σύμβολον ὁρῶν σῆς τέχνης ἀνεπίληπτον, εἰκόνι τύπου τετηρημένον, πεντάδι λυθὲν σῶμα· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι, πάτερ, συνέστω.“ ἑξῆς δὲ αὐτῷ τὸν Ἀσταφαιὸν, ᾧ πιστεύουσι τοιαῦτα ἐρεῖν· „τρίτης ἄρχων πύλης Ἀσταφαιὲ, ἐπίσκοπε πρώτης ὕδατος ἀρχῆς, ἕνα βλέπων μύστην πάρες με παρθένου πνεύματι κεκαθαρμένον, ὁρῶν οὐσίαν κόσμου· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι. πάτερ, συνέστω.“ μετὰ δ᾿ αὐτὸν τὸν Αἰλωαιὸν, ᾧ τοιαῦτα λέγειν οἴονται· „δευτέρας ἄρχων πύλης Αἰλωαιὲ, πάρες με τῆς σῆς μητρὸς φέροντά σοι σύμβολον, χάριν κρυπτομένην δυνάμεσιν ἐξουσιῶν· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι, πάτερ, συνέστω.“ τελευταῖον δὲ τὸν Ὡραῖον ὀνομάζουσι καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγειν οἴονται· „ὑπερβὰς φραγμὸν πυρὸς ἀφόβως. πρώτης λαχὼν ἀρχὴν πύλης Ὡραῖς, πάρες με, σῆς ὁρῶν δυνάμεως σύμβολον καταλυθὲν τύπῳ ζωῆς ξύλου, εἰκόνι καθ᾿ ὁμοίωσιν ληφθὲν ἀθώου· ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι, πάτερ, συνέστω.“
pass_a_gloss: If anyone wishes to learn also the fictions (πλάσματα) of those sorcerers (γοήτων), by which they wished to bring people under (ὑπάγειν) their teaching as having certain secrets (ἀπόρρητα), but were not quite able (οὐ πάνυ ἐδυνήθησαν), let him hear what they are taught to say after passing through what they name 'the barrier of evil' (φραγμὸν κακίας), gates of the archons bound by/for an age (αἰῶνι δεδεμένας): 'Solitary/single-natured king (βασιλέα μονότροπον), bond of blindness (δεσμὸν ἀβλεψίας), unheeding oblivion (λήθην ἀπερίσκεπτον), I greet (ἀσπάζομαι), first power (πρώτην δύναμιν), kept (τηρουμένην) by spirit of providence (πνεύματι προνοίας) and by wisdom (σοφίᾳ); from there I am sent pure (εἰλικρινής), already a part of light of Son and Father; let grace be with me (ἡ χάρις συνέστω μοι), yes Father, let it be with me.' And they say the beginnings/principalities (ἀρχάς) of the Ogdoad (ὀγδοάδος) are from here. Then they are taught to say, passing through whom they call Ialdabaoth: 'You, with confidence (μετὰ πεποιθήσεως), first and seventh, born to rule (γεγονὼς κρατεῖν), Ialdabaoth, being ruling word (ἄρχων λόγος) of a pure mind (νοὸς εἰλικρινοῦς), perfect work (ἔργον τέλειον) for Son and Father, bearing a symbol (σύμβολον ἐπιφέρων) by the stamp of a figure of life (χαρακτῆρι τύπου ζωῆς), having opened to the world the gate which you shut for/by your aeon (ἔκλεισας αἰῶνι σῷ), I pass by (παροδεύω) your authority (ἐξουσίαν) free again (ἐλεύθερος πάλιν); grace be with me, yes Father, be with me.' They say the star Phaenon (Φαίνοντα) sympathises (συμπαθεῖν) with the lion-shaped archon. Then they think one who has passed Ialdabaoth and reached Iao must say: 'You, ruler of hidden mysteries of Son and Father, night-shining (νυκτοφαής), second Iao and first, master of death (δέσποτα θανάτου), part of the guiltless (μέρος ἀθώου), bearing now my own beard (ὑπήνην) as symbol, passing by your rule ready (ἕτοιμος); you overpowered/strengthened (κατίσχυσας) the one born from you by a living word (λόγῳ ζῶντι); grace be with (me), Father, be with.' Next Sabaoth, to whom they think they will say: 'Ruler of the fifth authority, potentate (δυνάστα) Sabaoth, advocate (προήγορε) of the law of your creation being loosed (λυομένης) by grace, by a more powerful pentad (πεντάδι δυνατωτέρᾳ), let me pass (πάρες με), seeing the unblameable (ἀνεπίληπτον) symbol of your art (τέχνης), kept by an image of a figure, a body loosed by a pentad; grace be with me, Father, be with me.' Next to him Astaphaeus, to whom they trust they will say: 'Ruler of the third gate, Astaphaeus, overseer (ἐπίσκοπε) of the first beginning/source of water (πρώτης ὕδατος ἀρχῆς), seeing one initiate (ἕνα βλέπων μύστην), let me pass, cleansed by spirit of a virgin, seeing the substance of the world (οὐσίαν κόσμου); grace be with me, Father, be with me.' After him Ailoaeus, to whom they think to say: 'Ruler of the second gate, Ailoaeus, let me pass, bringing you a symbol of your mother, grace hidden by the powers of the authorities (δυνάμεσιν ἐξουσιῶν); grace be with me, Father, be with me.' Last they name Horaeus and think to say to him: 'Having stepped over (ὑπερβάς) the barrier of fire fearlessly (ἀφόβως), having been allotted (λαχών) the rule of the first gate, Horaeus, let me pass, seeing the symbol of your power undone (καταλυθέν) by a figure of the tree of life (τύπῳ ζωῆς ξύλου), taken in an image after likeness (εἰκόνι καθ᾿ ὁμοίωσιν) of a guiltless one (ἀθώου); grace be with me, Father, be with me.'
pass_b_english: If anyone wishes to learn the inventions of those sorcerers as well, by which they wanted to draw people into their teaching as though they possessed certain secrets, though they were not really able to do so, let him hear what they are taught to say after passing through what they call “the barrier of evil”, the gates of the archons, bound for ever: “I greet the solitary king, the bond of blindness, heedless forgetfulness, the first power, kept by the spirit of providence and by wisdom. From there I am sent forth pure, already a part of the light of the Son and the Father. May grace be with me; yes, Father, may it be with me.” And they say that the beginnings of the Ogdoad lie here.

Next, as they pass through the one they call Ialdabaoth, they are taught to say: “And you, Ialdabaoth, first and seventh, born to rule with confidence, being the ruling word of a pure mind, a perfect work for the Son and the Father: I bring a symbol stamped with the figure of life, and I have opened to the world the gate that you shut for your aeon. Free once more, I pass by your dominion. May grace be with me; yes, Father, may it be with me.” And they say that the star Phaenon is in sympathy with the lion-shaped archon.

Then they think that whoever has passed Ialdabaoth and reached Iao must say: “And you, ruler of the hidden mysteries of the Son and the Father, who shine by night, second Iao and first master of death, portion of the innocent one: bearing now my own beard as a symbol, I pass by your rule, ready. By a living word you have overpowered the one who came forth from you. May grace be present, Father, may it be present.”

Next comes Sabaoth, to whom they think they will say: “Ruler of the fifth authority, mighty Sabaoth, advocate of the law of your creation, a creation being undone by grace, by a mightier pentad: let me pass, seeing the blameless symbol of your art, kept safe by the image of a figure, a body set free by the pentad. May grace be with me, Father, may it be with me.”

After him comes Astaphaeus, to whom they believe they will say such things as these: “Ruler of the third gate, Astaphaeus, overseer of the first source of water, looking on one initiate, let me pass, cleansed by the spirit of a virgin, seeing the substance of the world. May grace be with me, Father, may it be with me.”

After him comes Ailoaeus, to whom they think they are to say such things as these: “Ruler of the second gate, Ailoaeus, let me pass, as I bring you the symbol of your mother, a grace hidden by the powers of the authorities. May grace be with me, Father, may it be with me.”

Last they name Horaeus, and they think they are to say to him: “I have crossed the barrier of fire without fear. You who were allotted the rule of the first gate, Horaeus, let me pass, seeing the symbol of your power undone by a figure of the tree of life (Genesis 2:9), taken in an image after the likeness of an innocent one (Genesis 1:26). May grace be with me, Father, may it be with me.”

choices.choice: These are the Ophite formulae Origen adds himself; they are not Celsus’s words, and their Greek is obscure and probably corrupt in places, so the English stays close to the wording and keeps its ambiguities. Son and Father capitalised because the formulae mean by them the highest God and His Son; the archons’ titles (‘ruling word’, ‘king’) are left lower case. αἰῶνι δεδεμένας: ‘bound for ever’ or ‘bound by an aeon’; αἰῶνι σῷ likewise ‘for/by your aeon’. τῆς ὀγδοάδος τὰς ἀρχάς: ‘the beginnings’ of the Ogdoad, possibly ‘the principalities’. Phaenon (Φαίνων) is the planet Saturn. In the Iao formula ὑπήνην (‘beard’) is doubtful as printed; the sense is unclear and it is rendered literally. κατίσχυσας is second person as printed (‘you have overpowered/strengthened’); a first-person κατίσχυσα would make better sense in the speaker’s mouth, but the printed text is kept. The Iao refrain lacks μοι, so it is rendered ‘May grace be present’. ἕνα βλέπων μύστην may mean ‘looking on a single initiate’ or ‘an initiate of the One’; participles ὁρῶν/βλέπων in the Sabaoth, Astaphaeus and Horaeus formulae agree with the archon addressed, not with the speaker; ὑπερβάς (Horaeus) is nominative and most naturally the speaker’s, so the participle is turned into a main verb (‘I have crossed’) to make the English stand as a sentence (Greek: a participial clause ending in a stop); nothing is added. In the Ialdabaoth formula the nominatives ἄρχων λόγος ὑπάρχων ... ἔργον τέλειον may describe either the archon (as rendered) or the speaker; the main verb παροδεύω and the participles ἐπιφέρων, ἀνοίξας are the speaker’s. In the Iao formula the order δεύτερε Ἰαὼ καὶ πρῶτε δέσποτα θανάτου is kept (‘second Iao and first master of death’); ἀρχή is ‘rule’, ἐξουσία ‘dominion’/’authority’. Ὡραῖς is printed for the vocative Ὡραῖε. The Horaeus formula echoes Genesis 2:9 (tree of life) and Genesis 1:26 (image and likeness) in Gnostic use; both cited inline as allusions, not quotations. ‘Ailoaeus’ (Αἰλωαιός) here differs from ‘Eloaeus’ (Ἐλωαῖος) in 6.32; both kept as printed.
Iao: Greek order kept, 'second Iao and first master of death'
ἀρχή 'rule', ἕτοιμος kept as 'ready' (was modal 'I am ready to pass')
Horaeus: removed added 'I come'; participle made main verb 'I have crossed'
